div.head: II Cn 74
div.ab: ⁊ na nyde man naðer ne wif ne mæden to þam, þe hyre sylfre mislicie, ne wið sceatte ne sylle, butan he hwæt agenes ðances gyfan wylle.
And ne nyde man næfre naðor ne wif ne mæden to ðam, þe hire sylfre mislicige, ne wið sceatte ne sylle, buton he hwæt agenes ðances gyfan wylle.
And ne nime man naðer ne wif ne mæden to þam, þe hyre sylfre mislicie, ne wið sceatte ne sylle, buton he hwæt agenes þances gyfan wylle.
Et numquam cogatur uirgo uel femina ad eum, qui sibi displiceat, nec pro pecunia detur, nisi idem aliquid sponte sua dare uelit.
Nemo cogat mulierem aut uirginem contra uoluntatem illarum, quod eis displiceat, nec pro pecunia nec pro alia re, nisi quis sponte quid dare uoluerit.
Nec quisquam cogat mulierem uiduam uel uirginem ad hoc quod sibi displiceat, neque pro censu uendat, nisi qu[i]d ipse sua sponte dare uelit.
And ne nyde man næfre naðor ne wif ne mæden to ðam þe hire sylfre mislicige, ne wið sceatte ne sylle, buton he hwæt agenes ðances gyfan wylle.
And na nyde man naðer ne wif ne mæden to þam þe hyre sylfre mislicie, ne wið sceatte ne sylle butan he hwæt agenes ðances gyfan wylle.

Und weder eine [verwittwete] Frau noch eine Jungfrau werde (jemals B) gezwungen (genommen A) zu dem [Manne], der ihr selbst missfällt, noch für Geld verkauft, ausser wenn der [Freier ihrem Vormund] aus eigenem Antriebe etwas schenken will.

And let neither a [widowed] woman nor a maiden (ever, B) be forced (taken, A) to [a man] who displeases her herself, nor sold for money, unless the [suitor] is willing of his own accord to give something [to her guardian].
And no woman or maiden shall ever be forced to marry a man whom she dislikes, nor shall she be given for money, except the suitor desires of his own freewill to give something.
And neither a widow nor a maiden is ever to be forced to marry a man whom she herself dislikes, nor to be given for money, unless he chooses to give anything of his own freewill.
And no woman or maiden shall ever be compelled to take a husband whom she dislikes, nor is money ever to be paid for her unless the suitor wishes to give something of his own free will.

note.seg: A's Sinn von nime ‘gewaltsam ergreifen, zwingend hinführen’ (Wb S. 157 Z. 1) scheint unbelegt. Vielleicht also bloss Schreibfehler für nide
A's sense of nime, ‘seize by force, lead off under compulsion’ (Wb p. 157 l. 1), seems to be unattested. Perhaps, therefore, merely a scribal error for nide
Vgl. Gl Eheschliessung 7c. 16d. i. n ff. Ergänze hier 16 m das Zitat Steenstrup Normannerne I 319. III 373
Cf. Gl Eheschliessung 7c. 16d. i. n ff. Add here at 16 m the reference Steenstrup Normannerne I 319. III 373
Neben Geldgewinn denkt an andere Vorteile, die der Brautkäufer gewährt, Inst
Besides monetary gain, Inst has in mind other advantages that the purchaser of the bride grants

Zunächst ist Verkäufer der Brautvormund aus ihrer Sippe, später der Gefolgsherr, in Normannenzeit der Lehnsherr.—Kemble sieht hierin mit Unrecht einen Verzicht des Königs auf Verkauf seines Heiratskonsenses; Saxons II 97

The seller is at first the bride's guardian from her kindred, later the lord of the following, in Norman times the feudal lord.—Kemble wrongly sees in this a renunciation by the king of the sale of his consent to marriage; Saxons II 97
Cf. Wifmannes Beweddung, 1; Earle, Land Charters, p. 228, where the marriage contract between a certain Godwine and his prospective father-in-law Byrhtric is given.
